dailyInsight.headline: Audit the required-compaction path before trusting an oversized Codex session
dailyInsight.insight: OpenClaw’s public issue and main-branch fix show a specific failure mode in which a required reply preflight accepted neither an intentional Codex app-server no-op nor a real compaction, then dropped the incoming turn. Operators using Codex app-server sessions should audit the installed version and a disposable budget-crossing path before assuming automatic compaction preserves the next message.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The issue traces a required preflight that received `ok: true, compacted: false` because the Codex app server owned automatic compaction, but the reply path classified that result as fatal. The follow-up change labels the request `required_preflight`, dispatches native compaction, and converts only missing or stale Codex bindings into an explicit recoverable failure for the existing context-engine fallback.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: The useful distinction is between a benign status and a completed recovery. If a system says compaction is required, accepting an uncompacted no-op can silently turn a context-management contract into lost user input. A bounded audit is safer than treating a main-branch repair as proof that all long-context sessions are reliable.

actions.audience: Operator or builder running OpenClaw with a Codex app-server harness
actions.label: Check the required-preflight handoff in a disposable session
actions.instruction: First identify whether the installed build contains the public required-preflight change. In a non-production session with no sensitive conversation state, cross the configured context budget once and verify that the next user turn reaches a model reply or produces a documented recoverable binding path. Preserve only redacted diagnostics; do not force compaction against a live customer or production session as this test.
actions.effort: 15 minutes to identify the build and plan the test; 30–60 minutes for a disposable reproduction

receipts.title: fix(agents): allow required-preflight native Codex compaction (#120197)
receipts.supports: Shows the public implementation changes that name required preflight, dispatch native Codex compaction, and preserve stale or missing thread bindings as recoverable failures rather than successful skips.

receipts.title: Codex app-server required-preflight compaction tests at commit 16cde04136
receipts.supports: Shows source-level regression tests that assert a required preflight starts native thread compaction and that a changed binding reports an explicit stale-thread failure for fallback handling.

confidence.basis: A fresh public issue, implementation change, and focused tests agree on one narrowly scoped Codex app-server failure and recovery contract. The action is an audit of a disposable path, not a claim that a release or every deployment has the repair.

dailyInsight.limitation: These are public issue, main-branch code, and test receipts. They do not establish an installed release, frequency across deployments, behavior for non-Codex harnesses, or safety of forcing compaction on a live conversation.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise or withdraw this call if a public released-path reproduction shows that the required-preflight route still drops an otherwise valid user turn after native compaction succeeds, or if the stated fallback allows a stale binding to bypass the existing context-engine recovery boundary.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a release note naming the patch and for an independent operator report that exercises the same required-preflight path with a real Codex app-server session and a redacted before-and-after outcome.
